method: Builds a haproxy.cfg from a frontend, one to four backends and up to six use_backend rules. Each server keeps a name, address, port, weight, optional maxconn and a check flag, and the page writes defaults with mode and timeouts, a fe_main frontend, one acl per rule, the use_backend lines in declaration order and a default_backend naming the first backend. Weight is relative: the manual states that every server receives a load proportional to its weight over the sum of all weights, the default is 1, the maximum is 256, and a weight of 0 keeps the server out of load balancing while still accepting persistent connections. Each server therefore reports its exact weight, its share of the backend total as a percentage to one decimal, and an expected count per 1,000 requests allocated by largest remainder so the column sums to 1,000; roundrobin and static-rr follow those weights, while leastconn, source, uri and hdr do not and the page says so. Health checks use the manual's inter, fall and rise: a checked server is probed every inter milliseconds, marked down after fall consecutive failures and up again after rise successes, so the failover window is inter times fall and the recovery window is inter times rise, with defaults of 2000 ms, 3 and 2. The connection cap is the sum of the maxconn values that are set, and stays unset when none are. Routing rules offer path_beg, path_end, hdr(host) with a case-insensitive match and src; the manual evaluates use_backend rules in declaration order and the first match wins, otherwise default_backend applies, so a second rule with the same match and value is refused as unreachable, and content matches are refused in tcp mode because tcp does not parse request content. Names are limited to letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore starting with a letter, ports to 1-65535, weights to 0-256, maxconn to 1-1000000, inter to 1-60000 ms and fall and rise to 1-100; an all-numeric dotted address that is not a valid IPv4 literal is refused instead of being read as a host name. Not modelled: TLS termination, cookies and stick tables, DNS service discovery, ACL samples beyond these four, connection persistence, and whether the host runs HAProxy: the file has not been parsed by haproxy -c and the result does not deploy anything. Pure local text processing: no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: HAProxy 2.8 Configuration Manual, server and default-server options, weight: load is proportional to the weight over the sum of all weights, the default is 1, the maximum is 256, and 0 removes the server from load balancing.
HAProxy 2.8 Configuration Manual, server and default-server options, inter, fall and rise: the check interval defaults to 2000 ms, fall to 3 failures and rise to 2 successes.
HAProxy 2.8 Configuration Manual, balance: roundrobin and static-rr use each server in turns according to its weight, with a 4095-server limit for roundrobin.
HAProxy 2.8 Configuration Manual, use_backend: rules are evaluated in declaration order, the first match assigns the backend, and default_backend is used otherwise.
